clips.send: A friend forwards this to someone about to quit after one no, since 302 nos built Disneyland; awe.
clips.caption:
J.K. Rowling was rejected by 12 publishers before Harry Potter sold a single copy.

Walt Disney heard no 302 times trying to get financing for Disneyland. People told him it was a bonehead idea, that nobody would ever come.

He didn't listen. He had confidence in the dream, and he wasn't going to let anyone talk him out of it.

Kevin Trudeau says rejection was never proof they were wrong - it was just the toll on the way to something nobody else could see yet.

clips.send: Someone sends this to a friend whose art or side hustle gets ignored, as proof the world catches up late; awe.
clips.caption:
Vincent van Gogh sold exactly one painting in his entire lifetime, to a friend who only bought it to be nice.

He kept painting anyway. No gallery, no buyers, just the work. By the time he died he'd finished over 800 pieces.

Today his most expensive painting is valued at $142 million.

Kevin Trudeau tells this story to make one point: the market can be wrong about you for your whole life and still be wrong.

What's the one thing you quit on too early? Tell me below.

#kevintrudeau #vangogh #art #nevergiveup #millionaire #mindset

clips.send: Someone sends this to a friend who buys cheap things on repeat, as a nudge to buy once and stop; anxiety.
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau came out of prison with no money. The government had taken every penny he had.

But the clothes he'd bought 20 and 30 years earlier still fit, still buttoned, still looked sharp. The suit was 30 years old. The shoes were Aldens.

"They'll last 400 years," he says.

That's the whole lesson on quality: cheap stuff needs replacing forever, so you keep paying for it forever. Good stuff you buy once.
